caption: Fuel alone was R3 400 this month, more than the car instalment. Does the maths still work if you're driving full time?

slides.title:
How I spend
my R18 200
p/m income
Living in Newcastle
slides.body:
Male, 41
Divorced, daughter (15) every second weekend
Job: Full-time Bolt driver, owns his car
Net income: R18 200 p/m (this month)

slides.title: Car instalment
slides.includes: 2019 sedan, bought specifically for the platform
slides.body: This is the one bill that doesn't care whether it was a good week or a bad one.

slides.title: Fuel
slides.includes: Six days a week, mostly Newcastle and the run out to Ladysmith
slides.body: Some weeks this is bigger than the instalment. This was one of them.

slides.title: Insurance & tracking device
slides.includes: Comprehensive cover, required to stay on the platform
slides.body: Non-negotiable if I want to keep driving at all.

slides.title: Maintenance & tyres
slides.includes: A tyre replacement and a service, both due the same week
slides.body: I budget for this every month and it still catches me every time.

slides.title: Takeaways between shifts
slides.includes: Garage food, the odd KFC between fares
slides.body: I told myself it was R300. It's R700. Eating properly isn't easy on this schedule.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Room rent, groceries, phone & data, my daughter's things on my weekends, funeral policy, stokvel
slides.body: Everything that isn't the car, in one line. On an income that changes every week, this is the part I can't move.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R18 200 this month. Last month it was closer to R23 000. I never know which one I'm getting until the week's over.

slides.title: I stopped guessing between the good weeks and the bad ones
slides.body:
I upload my statement to Beyond Horizon every time the payouts land, even the thin weeks.

Seeing the fuel and maintenance against the actual fares finally showed me what I'm really taking home.

No bank login needed.
